question.leadin: Name some noteworthy popes of the Catholic Church.
question.text: This pope called for the First Crusade and offered a remission of sins for those who would participate in it.
question.answerHtml: Pope Urban II [accept Odo of Chatillon or Otho de Lagery; prompt on Urban]
question.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

swap.text: Martyrs and people who perform one miracle can receive this recognition, after which they earn the title of "blessed."
swap.clue: By what name is this process, which implies that the recipients are "blessed" by Heaven, called?

question.leadin: It was defined as the official Roman Catholic Dogma in the 1854 bull Ineffabilis Deus.
question.text: Identify this concept which states that Mary, the mother of Jesus, originated free from original sin.
question.clue: That bull, Ineffabilis Deus, was issued on the day of the "Feast" of this doctrine - December 8th - by Pope Pius IV.

swap.leadin: These documents were famously marketed by the weasely Johann Tetzel, who is quoted as saying regarding them: "every time a coin in the coffer rings, a soul from purgatory springs!"
swap.text: Name these documents, which forgave sins in exchange for money which was used to fund church buildings.
swap.clue: They were first granted en-masse during the Council of Clermont for those soldiers who set out to the Levant.

question.text: Savonarola was burned at the stake after dismissing the commands of Rodrigo Borgia, who at that time held this high religious title. The first person to hold this post was Peter.
question.answerHtml: pope [or equivalents like leader of the Catholic Church]
question.clue: Julius II was labeled the "warrior" one of these people after he formed the Holy League.

swap.text: The Society of Jesus was formally made part of the Catholic Church in 1540 by this pope, who also convened the Council of Trent.
swap.clue: This pope who assembled the Holy League decisively defeated by the Ottomans at the Battle of Preveza.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about an ecumenical council which began in 1869.
question.text: This religious council included the approval of the dogmatic constitutions of Dei Filius and Pastor aeternus.
question.clue: This meeting declared anathema on anyone who disbelieved in miracles, condemned all opposition to Ultramontanism, and enacted several principles first put forth in the Syllabus of Errors.

swap.text: The eighth pope of this name officially recognized witches' existence with a 1484 bull. The third pope of this name excommunicated King John and convened the fourth Lateran council.
swap.clue: Yet another pope by this name issued the bull Summis Desiderantes which targeted witchcraft, and threatened to excommunicate those who read the theses of Pico della Mirandola in Rome.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Great Schism of the West per part.
question.text: At the Council of Constance, this man was elected as sole holder of the papacy, thus ending the schism.
question.clue: This man was elected pope during the 1417 Council of Constance. The successor to Gregory XII, he ruled until 1431 when he was succeeded by Eugene IV.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the First Crusade for the stated points.
swap.text: For 10 points, this pope's Sermon of Clermont called for the crusade.
swap.answerHtml: Urban II [prompt on Urban; or Odo of Lagery] [10/15/20] 10 for one, 15 for two, and 20 for all three, name the three principalities established under the Kingdom of Jerusalem by the First Crusade. ANSWER: Antioch, Edessa, Tripoli
swap.clue: This leader wrote a letter of instruction to the Flemish mentioning Adhemar of Le Puy, as reported on by Baldric of Dol and Robert the Monk.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Counter Reformation.
question.text: This council preceding the one at Trent, started by Julius II and finished by Leo X, signaled the start of reformist attitudes, though it accomplished little in the way of actual church reform, instead dealing with the French Pragmatic Sanction and requiring permission to print books.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some really, really bad popes.
swap.text: Pope Sergius III initiated this period, which historians judge to be the nadir of the papacy. Also known as "saeculum obscurum," or "the dark age," its more colorful name refers to the influence wielded by women such as Sergius' mistress, Marozia, and her mother, Theodora.
swap.clue: In addition to John X, this period saw the reign of Lando, and much of the information known about this period comes from the writings of Liutprand of Cremona.

question.text: Clement VII was the first of two of these popes, who are not considered official by the Roman Catholic Church. Modern groups of them include the Sedevacantist ones and the Conclavist ones.
question.clue: The last generally recognized one of these was Felix V, who reigned in the 1440s. Another one was patronized by the Crescentii and twice seized power as Boniface VII.

swap.text: This pope was the best-known advocate of Lublin Thomism, which he learned at the Catholic University of Lublin in his native Poland. He denounced abortion and capital punishment in Evangelium Vitae.
swap.answerHtml: John Paul II [or Karol Wojtyla; or Ioannes Paulus II; or Giovanni Paolo II; or Jan Paweł II; prompt on any of the aforementioned names that do not include "the second"; do not accept or prompt on answers with just "John" or "Paul"]
swap.clue: This man survived an assassination attempt by the Turkish Mehmet Ali Agca, whom he later forgave.

question.text: The appointment of the fifth and last pope of this name at the Council of Constance ended the Western Schism.
question.clue: One pope of this name, whose love for Lake Bolsena eels and Vernaccia wine was lampooned in the Divine Comedy, was a Frenchman who ordered the Aragonese crusade against Peter III for overthrowing Charles of Anjou in the Sicilian Vespers.

swap.leadin: In an attempt to restore his faltering reputation, this man roped Jews into participating in the rigged Disputation of Tortosa and issued a papal bull banning them from making crucifixes or binding books.
swap.text: Name this Aragonese cardinal who maintained his antipope status for a staggering twenty-eight years, because he refused to resign with his colleagues Gregory XII and John XXIII during the Council of Constance.
swap.answerHtml: Antipope Benedict XIII [or Pedro Martinez de Luna y Perez de Gotor; prompt on Benedict]

question.leadin: This pope studied at a Catalonian monastery, where he was introduced to Arabic numerals.
question.text: Identify this pope who was credited with reintroducing the abacus and armillary sphere to Europe. He chose his papal name in honor of the pope who supposedly received the Donation of Constantine.
question.clue: This man was the first French pope and named himself after an earlier pope who, according to the forged Donation of Constantine, was given temporal power over the Western Roman Empire.

swap.text: Much of the discussion at Ferrara-Florence centered upon this Latin phrase, whose presence in the Nicene Creed was rejected by the Eastern Orthodox church. It describes the origin of the Holy Spirit.
swap.clue: The addition in question was this clause in the Nicene creed which translates to "from the Father and the Son." In greek, this clause had a literal one iota difference from the Orthodox preferred version.

question.text: The untrained Lombards that fought in this campaign were escorted across the Balkans, only to break into Alexius's palace at Blachernae and kill his pet lion. Kilij Arslan I destroyed William of Aquitaine's army during this successor to the First Crusade.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the career of Peter II of Aragon, FTPE.
swap.text: Peter was crowned in Rome by this man, born Lotario de Conti di Segni; he decreed the Fourth Crusade, initiated the pursuit of the Albigensians, and wrote the tract On the Miserable Condition of Man.
swap.clue: During a council called by this Pope, clergymen were forbidden from being involved in trials by ordeal, and Jews were mandated to wear identifying clothing.
